newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand aims to sell Bangkok BoC stake by March.
newsitem.headline: Thailand aims to sell Bangkok BoC stake by March.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Tuesday the government would sell 51 percent of its 65 percent stake in troubled Bangkok Bank of Commerce Plc (BBC) by March 1997.

Amnuay told a press conference Thai and foreign investors would be invited to bid for a majority stake of the bank after negotiations with Sitca Investment and Securities Plc fell through early this month.
Sitca offered to buy the bank shares at 20 baht ($0.80) each against 32 baht asked by the government.
"The BBC problems have dragged on for seven months. We want to get rid of this thorn in the neck quickly," Amnuay said.
The government of former Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa took over the bank last May after the disclosure of its big non-performing loan portfolio triggered a public run on its deposits.

Amnuay said the central bank, through its Fund for Rehabilitation of Financial Institutions, would seek to sell the majority of the bank's 10-baht shares at a still undetermined price of more than 30 baht, which would raise about 54 billion baht for the authorities.
He said buyers could pay for the bank stake in instalments of up to seven years.

The minister said the bank fund would use proceeds raised from the share sale to absorb the bank's 85 billion baht non-performing loans so that its new investors can take it over with a clean balance sheet.
He said under the arrangement, the new owners of Bangkok Bank of Commerce could make the bank profitable after the first year of their takeover.
Amnuay said the government would work towards boosting market confidence in the Thai banking and financial sector.

He said most Thai banks were healthy and profitable while the position of finance and securities firms would partly depend on the performance of the Thai bourse which has faced severe setbacks this year.
